newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania c.bank assets fall in January.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania c.bank assets fall in January.

text.p: The assets of Lithuania's central bank fell to 3.53 billion litas in January from 3.812 billion litas in December, the bank said on Tuesday.
The bank at the start of February announced that its official reserves fell to $793.2 million in January from $834.2 million at the end of December.
Foreign assets comprised 90 percent of the bank's assets at the end of January compared with 87.7 percent in December.
The bank added in a statement that it withdrew 75.1 million litas from circulation in January by selling U.S. dollars to and purchasing them from commercial banks.
This left 1.90 billion litas outside the central bank, of which 95.6 percent was in circulation and 4.4 percent was in commercial banks.
The central bank also said that the assets of Lithuania's commercial banks fell in January to 6.57 billion litas from 6.71 billion litas at end December.
Registered share capital for banks remained unchanged at 762.00 million litas in January.
Loans granted fell in January to 4.04 billion litas from 4.12 billion litas but deposits rose to 4.999 billion litas during January from 4.811 billion litas in December.
The bank also said that the percentage of loans compared with assets in Lithuania's banking system inched up to 61.5 percent in January from 61.4 percent at the end of December.
